title: Vibe Editing System
tagline: Direct the vibe. Let AI do the keyframes.
description: Make reels, ads, motion graphics, animation, VFX, AI films, soundtracks and bulk personalised videos by directing AI in plain language. No timeline, no keyframes.

modules.title: Getting Started
modules.summary: From zero to your first AI-edited video in one sitting. Install the tools, understand the Vibe Loop, and ship a 30-second edit today.
modules.outcome: You have Claude Code + the Vibe Editing Skills installed and a finished 30-second video exported for Reels.
modules.assignment: Make a 30-second edit of any clip on your phone using only prompts. Post the before/after in the community with the hashtag #MyFirstVibeEdit.

lessons.title: Welcome: what Vibe Editing actually is
lessons.summary: The new way to edit: you direct in plain words, AI builds the edit in code. See real before/afters made with this exact system.
lessons.prompt: Explain what you can do for me as my video editor, in 5 bullet points, then show me the menu of video types I can make.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Vibe Editing = you are the director, AI is the editor.** You describe the vibe ("warm, punchy, a little dreamy") and the AI writes and runs the edit.
- Nothing is dragged on a timeline. Every cut, caption, animation and sound is a line of code, so changes are instant: "make the title land on the beat" is one sentence.
- What you'll be able to make by the end: reels, ads, motion graphics, animations, VFX, AI films, soundtracks and hundreds of personalised videos.
- What you still bring: taste, the story, the footage, and the final yes. **Taste is the new skill.**
- Mindset for this course: *don't learn buttons, learn to direct.*

lessons.title: The toolkit: Claude Code, Python, ffmpeg (and why no timeline)
lessons.summary: A plain-English tour of the 3 tools behind every video in this course and what each one does for you.
lessons.prompt: Check my computer for everything Vibe Editing needs and tell me what's missing in plain English.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Claude Code**: the AI that reads your request, writes the editing code, runs it, and checks the result. Works in the terminal, desktop app or VS Code.
- **Python**: the language the edits are written in. You will *never* have to write it yourself.
- **ffmpeg**: the engine that actually cuts, encodes and exports video. Installed automatically.
- **The Skills Pack**: Ideabro's ready-made playbooks that tell Claude exactly how to make each type of video professionally.
- Why code instead of a timeline: repeatable, versioned, instantly editable, works for 1 video or 1,000.

lessons.title: Install everything in 15 minutes
lessons.summary: Step-by-step install on Mac and Windows: Claude Code, Python, and the Vibe Editing Skills Pack, with a live troubleshooting walk-through.
lessons.prompt: Let's make a video with the Vibe Editing System. Run the setup check and install anything missing.
lessons.notes_md:
1. Install Claude Code (desktop app or `npm install -g @anthropic-ai/claude-code`).
2. Install Python 3.10+ from python.org (Windows: tick **"Add Python to PATH"**).
3. Install the Skills Pack: unzip into `~/.claude/skills/` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\`), or install as a plugin.
4. Open Claude Code in an empty folder and say: *"Let's make a video with the Vibe Editing System."*
5. Claude runs `doctor.py`, installs what's missing, and shows test frames. **If you see the branded test frames, you're ready.**
- Windows tip: use `py` where guides say `python3`.
- "Externally managed environment" error → ask Claude: *"set up a virtual environment and re-run the doctor."*

lessons.title: Your first edit in 10 minutes
lessons.summary: Live: one phone clip in, a captioned and music-backed reel out. Copy the exact prompt and do it alongside.
lessons.prompt: Make a 30-second Instagram reel from raw/take1.mp4. Cut the pauses and ums, add big pop captions, upbeat music under my voice, and export for Reels.
lessons.notes_md:
- Drop your clip into the project's `raw/` folder (never edit originals; the system won't either).
- Claude will ask a few quick questions. Answering **"defaults are fine"** is allowed.
- Watch for the **contact sheet**: a grid of frames Claude shows you before calling anything done.
- Your files land in `out/`. The `_reels.mp4` version is ready to upload.
- 🎯 Win condition: a finished video you didn't touch a timeline for.

lessons.title: The Vibe Loop: Brief → Stills → Draft → Final
lessons.summary: The 7-step loop every professional Vibe Editor follows, and why it saves you hours of revisions.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Brief:** say what, who it's for, where it plays, the vibe.
- **Beat table:** a time-by-time plan (what we see / hear / read). Approve it *before* rendering.
- **Build:** AI writes the edit; all timings live in one file.
- **Stills:** check frames in seconds. Fix layout here, not after a 10-minute render.
- **Draft:** fast low-res version for timing.
- **Final:** full quality, checked again.
- **Export:** one command → every platform.
- Rule: **never approve what you haven't seen as stills.**

lessons.title: Your project folder & versioning (your undo button)
lessons.summary: How every project is organised, where your files go, and how versions keep you safe with clients.
lessons.notes_md:
| folder | what lives there |
|---|---|
| `raw/` | your originals (read-only) |
| `assets/` | logos, cut-outs, licensed music |
| `work/` | drafts, transcripts, intermediate files |
| `out/` | finished videos + review stills |
| `brief.md` | the plan |
| `brand.json` | colours + fonts |
| `timeline.py` | every timing in one place |
- Name deliverables `name_v1.mp4`, `name_v2.mp4`. Never overwrite a version a client has seen.
- Ask Claude to *"log this revision in work/revisions.md"* so you always know what changed.

modules.title: Vibe Editing Skills Pack (Bonus)
modules.summary: 9 ready-made Claude skills that turn a sentence into a finished video. Install once, use in every module after this.
modules.outcome: All 9 skills installed and tested. You know which skill to use for any video a client asks for.
modules.assignment: Make one 10–20 second video with three different skills (e.g. a talking-head clip, a logo reveal and an AI voiceover) and post all three.

lessons.title: What skills are (and why they're a cheat code)
lessons.summary: Skills are expert playbooks for Claude. Here's how they turn "make me a reel" into a pro-level edit, every time.
lessons.notes_md:
- A **skill** is a folder of instructions + tools Claude loads automatically when your request matches it.
- Without skills, AI guesses. With skills, it follows **Ideabro's production playbook**: brief, beat table, stills check, mixing rules, export specs.
- Every skill is self-contained: scripts, guides and templates included. Install one or all nine.
- You don't call them by name (but you can). Just describe the video.

lessons.title: Install in 5 minutes (zip and plugin methods)
lessons.summary: Two ways to install: unzip into your skills folder, or one command as a Claude Code plugin.
lessons.notes_md:
**Zip method**
1. Download `vibe-editing-system-all.zip` from Course Resources.
2. Unzip so each skill folder sits in `~/.claude/skills/` (Windows: `%USERPROFILE%\.claude\skills\`).
3. Restart Claude Code → type `/skills` → you should see 9 `vibe-…` skills.

**Plugin method** (if your instructor shares the marketplace link)
```
/plugin marketplace add <owner>/<repo>
/plugin install vibe-editing-system@ideabro-studio
```
- Update later with `/plugin update` (plugin) or by replacing the folders (zip).

lessons.title: Your first video with the Start Here skill
lessons.summary: Let the Start Here skill pick the right playbook, set up your project and show test frames, all in one conversation.
lessons.prompt: Let's make a video with the Vibe Editing System. I want a 20-second promo for my Instagram page @myhandle. Use defaults.
lessons.notes_md:
- The Start Here skill (`vibe-editing-system`) shows a menu of 8 video types and asks what you have (footage? logo? voice?).
- It runs setup, creates the project and renders branded test frames in ~1 minute.
- Then it switches to the matching playbook automatically.
- Say **"teach me as you go"** and it explains every step. Perfect for learning.

lessons.title: Skill: Talking-Head & Creator Videos
lessons.summary: Reels from raw takes, podcast clips, YouTube edits, testimonials and course lessons, cut word-accurately.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-talking-head: make a 45-second reel from raw/take1.mp4, put my strongest line first as the hook, pop captions, punch-in jump cuts.
lessons.notes_md:
- Cuts silences, ums and retakes using a word-level transcript.
- Moves your best line to the front as the **hook**.
- Captions: pop / karaoke / clean / minimal, in your brand colours.
- Adds lower-thirds, stickers and music ducked under your voice.

lessons.title: Skill: Launch Videos & Ads
lessons.summary: Promos, product launches, social ads with variants, app demos rebuilt as crisp graphics.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-launch-ads: 25-second launch reel for my course "Vibe Editing", bold and punchy, end card ENROLL NOW, also give me 1:1 and 4:5 versions.
lessons.notes_md:
- Follows the launch formula: Hook → Problem → Reveal → Proof → CTA.
- Everything locked to the music's beat.
- Variants (hooks, formats, languages) are re-renders, not re-edits.

lessons.title: Skill: Motion Graphics
lessons.summary: Showreels, explainers, kinetic typography, logo reveals, infographics and transparent lower-third packs.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-motion-graphics: a 6-second logo reveal for assets/logo.png with an impact on the beat and a sparkle.
lessons.notes_md:
- Every frame is generated from code, so it's razor sharp at any size.
- Export **transparent packs** (ProRes 4444) to use in Premiere, CapCut or DaVinci.
- Style frames first, animation second.

lessons.title: Skill: Stylised Animation
lessons.summary: Claymation, crayon, paper-cut, doodle and talking cartoon mascots with no AI images.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-stylised-animation: a 20-second claymation short about a sheep who discovers vibe editing at 2am. Wordless, playful music.
lessons.notes_md:
- Handmade feel from 3 tricks: **held drawings, boil, texture**.
- Characters blink, look and lip-sync to the voice automatically.

lessons.title: Skill: VFX & Editing Magic
lessons.summary: Background swaps, text behind you, layer splits, tracking, cinematic looks and slow motion.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-vfx: put the word VIBE in huge lime letters behind me in raw/take1.mp4, appearing when I say "vibe".
lessons.notes_md:
- Person cut-outs (mattes) in one command.
- Effects start on the exact word you speak.
- Honest feasibility check before promising a client an effect.

lessons.title: Skill: AI Footage → Films
lessons.summary: Turn Veo/Sora/Kling clips into a film that doesn't look AI, plus faceless channel episodes.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-ai-footage: scan the clips in raw/, tell me which are usable, then cut a 60-second brand film to my voiceover raw/vo.mp3.
lessons.notes_md:
- Scans every clip for morphs, garbled text and popping objects.
- Retimes shots to land on the narration.
- One grade + grain + sound design so it stops looking like AI.

lessons.title: Skill: Audio, Music & Voiceover
lessons.summary: Original copyright-free music, 14 sound effects, AI voiceover (incl. Hindi), audiograms and visualisers.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-audio-videos: make a chill 30-second music bed and a Hindi AI voiceover of my script in work/script.txt.
lessons.notes_md:
- 7 music moods: upbeat, hype, tech, corporate, chill, cinematic, playful.
- Auto-ducking: music dips when someone talks.
- Final mix hits platform loudness (−14 LUFS) automatically.

lessons.title: Skill: Bulk & Automated Videos
lessons.summary: 100 personalised videos from a spreadsheet, every format in one go, multi-language versions.
lessons.prompt: Use vibe-bulk-videos: make a personalised welcome video for every row in students.csv using their first_name.
lessons.notes_md:
- Build one hero template → test 3 rows → render the rest.
- Long names auto-fit. Non-English names supported with the right fonts.
- A report shows every video that rendered (and any that failed).

lessons.title: Updates & what's new
lessons.summary: Where new skill versions are announced and how to update in 1 minute.
lessons.notes_md:
- New versions are announced in the community and added to Course Resources.
- **Zip install:** delete the old `vibe-…` folders and unzip the new ones.
- **Plugin install:** run `/plugin update`.
- Changelog
  - **v1.0**: 9 skills, 20 tools, Ideabro house style, 7 music moods, 14 SFX, 4 caption styles.

modules.title: The Director's Brief
modules.summary: The skill that separates "AI slop" from professional work: telling the AI exactly what you want, in words it can execute.
modules.outcome: You can write a brief and a beat table that gets the edit right on the first render.
modules.assignment: Write a full brief + beat table for a 25-second promo of your own (or a dream client's) product. Share it for feedback before you render.

lessons.title: Anatomy of a great brief
lessons.summary: The 7 decisions every video needs. Make them up front and revisions drop by half.
lessons.notes_md:
1. **Goal**: what should the viewer think, feel or do?
2. **Audience**: who exactly, and where are they watching?
3. **Platform + format**: Reels 9:16? YouTube 16:9? Both?
4. **Length**: target and hard limit.
5. **Message**: hook, max 3 points, one CTA.
6. **Vibe**: 3 words + references.
7. **Brand**: colours, fonts, logo, handle.
- Template prompt: *"Here's my brief: [paste]. Ask me anything missing in one message, with defaults."*

lessons.title: Beat tables: plan every second
lessons.summary: The pro planning tool: a time-by-time table of what we see, hear and read. Get it approved before you render.
lessons.prompt: Draft a beat table for this video with columns time | what we see | what we hear | on-screen text. Keep cuts on the beat.
lessons.notes_md:
| time | picture | sound | text |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0.0–2.0 | face close-up, punch-in | impact | STOP SCROLLING |
| 2.0–6.0 | problem montage | whoosh + bed | HOURS PER REEL |
- Every row = one idea. If a row has two ideas, split it.
- Approving a beat table takes 2 minutes. Re-rendering takes 10.

lessons.title: Speaking "vibe": style vocabulary
lessons.summary: Translate feelings into instructions: what "premium", "punchy", "dreamy" and "cinematic" mean technically.
lessons.notes_md:
| you say | the AI does |
|---|---|
| punchy | hard cuts on beats, slams, impacts, 0.2–0.4 s moves |
| premium | slow moves, lots of space, serif titles, muted palette |
| playful | bounce/overshoot, bright colours, pops, glockenspiel |
| cinematic | letterbox, teal-orange grade, slow push-ins, drones |
| dreamy | soft focus, glow, slow fades, pastel, chill bed |
| techy | mono fonts, grids, glitch, scan lines, tech bed |
- Combine 2–3 words max. Contradictions ("calm but frantic") confuse every editor, human or AI.

lessons.title: References & brand kits
lessons.summary: How to describe a reference video so the AI copies the *feel*, not the content, and how to set up a brand in one file.
lessons.notes_md:
- Describe references as: **pace, type, colour, motion, sound**. E.g. *"pace like a MrBeast intro, type like Apple keynotes."*
- `brand.json` holds colours + fonts. Swap it and every video re-skins.
- No brand? The **Ideabro house style** is the default: ink, paper, lime.

lessons.title: Feedback that works
lessons.summary: The phrasing that gets a fix in one round: timestamps, specifics, and one change at a time.
lessons.prompt: At 0:04.2 the title lands late. Put it on the beat. Captions one size smaller and 10% higher.
lessons.notes_md:
- ❌ "Make it better" → ✅ "The hook needs more energy: faster cut at 0:01 and an impact sound."
- Always include **where** (timestamp), **what** (element), **how** (direction).
- Batch small notes into one message; send big direction changes alone.

lessons.title: Reviewing with stills & contact sheets
lessons.summary: How to review a 60-second video in 10 seconds using contact sheets, and what to look for.
lessons.notes_md:
- Ask: *"Give me a contact sheet of the final with 12 frames."*
- Check: text inside safe zones, no typos, faces not covered, brand colours, first frame strong.
- Approve stills → then watch the full video once for timing and sound.

modules.title: Talking-Head Editing
modules.summary: The money module. Raw takes into scroll-stopping reels, podcast clips and YouTube videos: the edits clients pay for every week.
modules.outcome: You can turn any talking-head recording into a tight, captioned, music-backed reel and a YouTube edit.
modules.assignment: Record a 2–3 minute take about anything you know well. Deliver a 45-second reel (9:16) and a clean 16:9 cut with subtitles.

lessons.title: Transcribe: every word, timestamped
lessons.summary: How Whisper turns speech into word-level timestamps, the foundation of every precise talking-head edit.
lessons.prompt: Transcribe raw/take1.mp4. My name is Priya Sharma and my brand is Ideabro, so spell those right.
lessons.notes_md:
- Runs locally and free. First run downloads the model once.
- Give names and jargon up front ("--prompt") so they're spelled right.
- Read `work/transcript.txt`. That's your paper edit. Fix spellings before captions.

lessons.title: Story edit: find the hook, kill the retakes
lessons.summary: Edit from the transcript, not the timeline: pick the hook, drop retakes, tighten tangents, end on the payoff.
lessons.prompt: Read the transcript. Suggest the strongest hook line, list retakes to remove, and propose a 45-second cut. Don't render yet.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Hook** = bold claim, surprising number, question or result. It goes in the first 2 seconds, even if you said it at minute 2.
- **Retakes**: keep the *last complete* version of a repeated sentence.
- Cut "so, um, hey guys" intros. Start mid-energy.
- End on the payoff or CTA. Cut everything after.

lessons.title: Cut dead air, ums & retakes
lessons.summary: Word-accurate silence cutting with natural breathing room, and how to tune pace for Reels vs YouTube.
lessons.prompt: Cut the silences and filler words. Snappy social pace. Move my hook to the front and remove the retake at 12–15 seconds.
lessons.notes_md:
| pace | gap setting | use for |
|---|---|---|
| frantic | 0.25 s | hype reels |
| snappy | 0.35 s | Reels/TikTok (default) |
| natural | 0.5 s | YouTube, testimonials |
- Words keep a little padding so nothing gets clipped mid-syllable.

lessons.title: Jump cuts & punch-in zooms
lessons.summary: The classic creator look: zoom 8–15% on every other cut, centred on your face.
lessons.notes_md:
- Punch-ins hide jump cuts and add energy.
- 1.08–1.12 = subtle, 1.15+ = aggressive.
- Anchor the zoom on the face (usually ~38% from the top). Check stills so the head isn't cropped.

lessons.title: Animated captions that people actually read
lessons.summary: Pop, karaoke, clean and minimal styles: when to use each, sizing, safe zones and emphasis words.
lessons.prompt: Add pop captions in my brand colours, highlight the words "free", "secret" and "10x", and keep them above the bottom 420 pixels.
lessons.notes_md:
- Most social video is watched with the sound off. **Captions are not optional.**
- **Pop**: 1–3 big words, active word highlighted (Reels/TikTok).
- **Karaoke**: line fills as spoken (lyrics, quotes).
- **Clean**: sentence subtitles on a soft box (YouTube, interviews).
- **Minimal**: small outlined (cinematic, brand films).
- Never cover the mouth or eyes. Also deliver the `.srt` file for YouTube/LinkedIn.

lessons.title: Lower-thirds, B-roll & stickers
lessons.summary: Graphics that sit on top of your footage: name titles, emoji pops, progress bars and CTA cards, timed to your words.
lessons.prompt: Add a lower-third with my name and title in the first 3 seconds, a 🔥 sticker that pops when I say "money", and a CTA card at the end.
lessons.notes_md:
- Graphics render as a **transparent overlay** and are laid on top, so long videos stay fast.
- Time every graphic to a word in the transcript.
- One graphic at a time. Clutter kills retention.

lessons.title: Podcast → 5 viral clips
lessons.summary: Find the best self-contained moments in a long recording, reframe to vertical, caption and export a batch.
lessons.prompt: Here's a 40-minute podcast in raw/. Find the 5 best 30–60 second clips, give me a table with timestamps, title and hook line, then render the ones I pick.
lessons.notes_md:
- A good clip: strong first line, makes sense alone, has emotion or a useful insight, ≤ 60 s.
- Two-person podcasts: crop on whoever's speaking, or use a blurred-background vertical.
- Batch export: Reels + Shorts + TikTok in one command.

lessons.title: YouTube long-form, testimonials & course lessons
lessons.summary: Three more paying formats: chapters + clean captions for YouTube, warm testimonials, and screen + face-cam lessons.
lessons.notes_md:
- **YouTube:** natural pace, punch-in every 5–10 s, chapters from the transcript, subtitles file, graphic every 20–40 s.
- **Testimonial:** gentle cuts, warm grade, name lower-third, chill bed at low volume.
- **Course lesson:** screen recording + round face-cam bubble, zoom into the action, callouts on key clicks.

modules.title: Sound Design & Music in Code
modules.summary: Sound is half the video. Generate original, copyright-free music, sound effects and voiceovers, and mix like a pro.
modules.outcome: You can score any video with an original bed, place SFX on the right frames, add an AI voiceover and deliver a broadcast-clean mix.
modules.assignment: Take any silent video (or one from the Talking-Head module) and give it a full soundtrack: music, 4+ sound effects, ducking and a −14 LUFS master.

lessons.title: Why we synthesise: no copyright strikes, ever
lessons.summary: Why using trending audio in client work is risky, and how generated music solves it forever.
lessons.notes_md:
- Music from YouTube/Spotify/TikTok libraries in client deliverables = Content ID claims, muted videos, angry clients.
- The Skills Pack *generates* original music and SFX in code, so they're yours to use commercially.
- Client has a licensed track? Use it, keep the licence note in the project.

lessons.title: Music moods, BPM & the beat grid
lessons.summary: 7 moods, how tempo shapes energy, and the simple math that makes every cut land on the beat.
lessons.prompt: Make a 30-second hype music bed at 128 BPM and plan my cuts on the bar lines.
lessons.notes_md:
| mood | BPM | use for |
|---|---|---|
| upbeat | 118 | creators, tutorials |
| hype | 128 | ads, reveals |
| tech | 124 | SaaS, AI |
| corporate | 110 | brand, LinkedIn |
| chill | 84 | vlogs, calm talking heads |
| cinematic | 72 | brand films, trailers |
| playful | 120 | kids, food, fun |
- **beat = 60 ÷ BPM.** At 128 BPM: 1 beat = 0.469 s, 1 bar = 1.875 s, 30 s = 16 bars.
- Cut on bars, accent on beats.

lessons.title: The SFX vocabulary
lessons.summary: 14 sound effects and exactly when to use each so your edits feel expensive.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Whoosh**: transitions (start 0.3 s *before* the cut).
- **Pop**: text and stickers appearing.
- **Impact / bass drop**: hooks, reveals, title slams.
- **Riser**: build into the big moment.
- **Click / typing**: UI, prompts.
- **Sparkle / ding**: magic, success.
- 3–6 accents per 30 s. More = noise.

lessons.title: AI voiceover (English, Hindi & more)
lessons.summary: Natural local AI voices for explainers, ads and faceless content, line by line, with timings.
lessons.prompt: Turn work/script.txt into a voiceover with a warm female voice at normal speed, then give me word timings.
lessons.notes_md:
- Write as people speak: short sentences, numbers in words, acronyms spelled out ("A.I.").
- One line per take, so you can regenerate a single line without redoing everything.
- Hindi voices included. Always have a native speaker listen once.

lessons.title: Mixing: ducking, levels & loudness
lessons.summary: Voice on top, music under, SFX accents, and a final master at platform loudness. All automatic, once you know the rules.
lessons.notes_md:
| element | level |
|---|---|
| voice | 0 dB (reference) |
| music under voice | −8 to −12 dB, ducked 10 dB while speaking |
| SFX | −6 to −12 dB (impacts up to −3) |
| final master | −14 LUFS social, −16 LUFS podcast/web |
- Listen on phone speakers *and* headphones before delivery.

lessons.title: Fix bad audio
lessons.summary: Clean up noisy phone audio: high-pass, denoise, compression and de-essing in one command.
lessons.prompt: Clean up the voice in raw/take1.mp4: remove background hiss and harsh S sounds, then re-mix with a chill bed.
lessons.notes_md:
- Fixes: hiss, rumble, uneven volume, harsh "S" sounds.
- Can't fully fix: heavy echo, music bleeding under speech, clipping. **Re-record if possible.**
- Recording tip for students: a ₹500 lav mic beats any AI cleanup.

modules.title: Launch Videos
modules.summary: Videos that sell. Promos, product launches and social ads with a clear hook, one message and a CTA, all locked to the beat.
modules.outcome: You can produce a 25-second launch reel plus format and hook variants ready for ads.
modules.assignment: Make a 25-second launch reel for a real or imaginary product, in 9:16 + 1:1, with 2 different hooks. Post both hooks and let the community vote.

lessons.title: The launch formula
lessons.summary: Hook → Problem → Reveal → Proof → CTA. The 25-second structure behind most ads that convert.
lessons.notes_md:
| beat | job | time |
|---|---|---|
| Hook | stop the scroll | 0–3 s |
| Problem | name the pain in their words | 3–7 s |
| Reveal | product/offer appears on a bar line | 7–11 s |
| Proof | 3 benefits max, numbers, faces | 11–20 s |
| CTA | what to do now | 20–25 s |
- One video = one message. Two messages = two videos.

lessons.title: Hooks that stop the scroll
lessons.summary: 10 proven hook patterns, how to animate each, and how to test them against each other.
lessons.prompt: Give me 5 hook options for my launch video, each with on-screen text and the visual, then render the top 2 as variants.
lessons.notes_md:
- Pattern interrupt: a crumpling timeline, a smash, a glitch.
- Bold claim: *"I made 10 reels in 1 hour."*
- Painful question: *"Still editing like it's 2015?"*
- Before/after split screen.
- A typed prompt + instant result (the vibe editing signature).
- The hook must work **muted**: big text + motion + contrast.

lessons.title: Building scenes: kinetic type, chips, counters
lessons.summary: The building blocks of every promo: slamming titles, benefit chips, counters, highlight bars and end cards.
lessons.prompt: Build scene 2 as three benefit chips that pop in on the beat: CUTS, CAPTIONS, MUSIC. Lime and periwinkle, mono font.
lessons.notes_md:
- Max 6 words per card, verbs first.
- Stagger builds by ~80 ms per item.
- Every pop gets a pop sound. Every reveal gets an impact.
- Check stills before animating.

lessons.title: Product hero shots & cut-outs
lessons.summary: Turn a product photo into a floating, shadowed hero shot with price and benefit callouts.
lessons.prompt: Cut out raw/product.jpg, make it float with a soft shadow and slow push-in, and add a price card "₹999 today only".
lessons.notes_md:
- One command removes the background from photos.
- Soft shadow + slight float + slow push-in = premium.
- Prices and claims exactly as the client wrote them.

lessons.title: App & SaaS demos (without blurry screen recordings)
lessons.summary: Rebuild the key screens as crisp vector UI inside a phone or laptop frame, then animate taps and typing.
lessons.notes_md:
- Screen recordings scaled up look soft. Rebuilt UI stays razor sharp in any format.
- Show 2–4 key screens only: the problem moment, the magic moment, the result.
- Animate: tap ripples, typing, highlight boxes, smooth screen transitions.

lessons.title: Variants: formats, hooks & cut-downs
lessons.summary: Turn one ad into 9:16, 4:5, 1:1, 16:9, two hooks, and 15 s + 6 s cut-downs without re-editing.
lessons.prompt: Render this ad in 9:16, 4:5 and 1:1, plus a 15-second cut-down with just hook, reveal and CTA.
lessons.notes_md:
- Design once in relative units → every format adapts. Check stills per format.
- 15 s = hook + reveal + CTA. 6 s bumper = logo hit + one line + CTA.
- Name files clearly: `brand_launch_hookA_9x16_v1.mp4`.

lessons.title: Event teasers, countdowns & testimonials
lessons.summary: Three bonus formats clients ask for: event/webinar teasers, countdowns, and testimonial compilations.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Teaser:** date-time card, speaker cards, "save your seat".
- **Countdown:** big numbers on beats, final number = impact + reveal.
- **Testimonial compilation:** face clips + quote cards in brand style, the best line first.

modules.title: Motion Graphics
modules.summary: Studio-quality motion design from a prompt: explainers, kinetic typography, logo reveals, infographics and transparent title packs.
modules.outcome: You can design style frames, animate them with professional timing and deliver motion packs other editors can use.
modules.assignment: Create a 20-second showreel with 4 sections (kinetic type, shapes, data, logo outro) in 16:9, plus one transparent lower-third.

lessons.title: Every frame is a function of time
lessons.summary: The one idea behind code-based motion design, and why it makes changes instant.
lessons.notes_md:
- Each frame is drawn from scratch for a moment `t`. Nothing is "keyframed".
- That's why you can render any single frame instantly (stills), render in parallel, and change timings without breaking anything.
- You direct in timings and feelings. The AI handles the math.

lessons.title: Style frames first, animation second
lessons.summary: Approve the look of each section as a still before animating. This is how studios avoid wasted renders.
lessons.prompt: Before animating, show me the key still of each section so I can approve the look.
lessons.notes_md:
- Most revisions are about **design** (layout, type, colour), not motion.
- Approve 3–5 stills → then animate.
- Keep max 2 typefaces and 1 accent colour per screen.

lessons.title: Easing & timing: why things feel alive
lessons.summary: Ease-out, back, expo, bounce, spring: what each communicates and the timing rules pros follow.
lessons.notes_md:
| intent | easing | duration |
|---|---|---|
| arrive | ease-out expo/cubic | 0.3–0.5 s |
| playful arrive | back / spring | 0.4–0.6 s |
| leave | ease-in | 0.2–0.35 s |
| move across | ease-in-out | 0.5–0.9 s |
- Exits are faster than entrances.
- Never linear for anything that starts or stops.

lessons.title: Kinetic typography
lessons.summary: Word slams, staggers, highlight bars, typewriters and masked reveals, synced to voice or beat.
lessons.prompt: Kinetic typography for my voiceover: each word slams in on the exact moment I say it, key words in lime with an impact sound.
lessons.notes_md:
- Sync to voice: transcribe → each word animates at its timestamp.
- Reading time: 0.3 s per word + 0.5 s.
- Emphasis = size, colour, or motion. Pick one per word.

lessons.title: Logo reveals & intros
lessons.summary: Build a 3–6 second logo reveal from shapes, masks and an impact sound.
lessons.prompt: Make a 5-second logo reveal: the logo assembles from 3 shapes, lands on the downbeat with an impact and sparkle, then the tagline types in.
lessons.notes_md:
- Split the logo into parts → animate in → land on the full logo + sound.
- Hold the final logo at least 1.5 s.
- Provide transparent and solid-background versions.

lessons.title: Data & infographic videos
lessons.summary: Animated bar charts, lines that draw on, counters and timelines with numbers that are always exact.
lessons.notes_md:
- Bars grow with ease-out. Lines draw on. Counters race with ease-out-expo.
- Label units and sources on screen.
- Numbers are copied exactly from the client. Never "rounded for style".

lessons.title: Transparent packs: lower-thirds, titles, transitions
lessons.summary: Export alpha-channel ProRes files you can sell or drop into Premiere, CapCut or DaVinci.
lessons.prompt: Make a pack of 5 transparent lower-thirds in my brand, each 4 seconds with in-hold-out animation, plus a preview sheet.
lessons.notes_md:
- Transparent = no background painted. Exported as ProRes 4444 `.mov`.
- One file per element, 3–6 s each.
- Check over dark AND light backgrounds. 💡 Packs are a sellable digital product.

lessons.title: Advanced: shaders & WebGL looks
lessons.summary: For liquid, glow and particle-heavy looks: render HTML/WebGL scenes headlessly into video.
lessons.notes_md:
- Use for GPU looks: liquid gradients, bloom, thousands of particles, 3D.
- Everything else: stick to the standard engine (simpler, faster).
- Needs a one-time browser install (`npx playwright install chromium`).

modules.title: Stylised Animation & Characters
modules.summary: Handmade looks without AI images: claymation, crayon, paper-cut and cartoon mascots that blink, bounce and talk.
modules.outcome: You can make a 30–40 second stylised short with a character, a story arc and cartoon sound design.
modules.assignment: Create a 30-second animated short in the medium of your choice (clay, crayon, paper or doodle) with a mascot that reacts to something. Wordless or narrated.

lessons.title: Faking a medium: held drawings, boil, texture
lessons.summary: The three tricks that make code look handmade, and why "smooth" is the enemy.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Held drawings:** animate at 12 drawings/second (on twos), not a smooth 24/30.
- **Boil:** outlines re-wobble slightly each drawing, like real clay or crayon.
- **Texture:** paper grain, clay thumbprints, crayon tooth.
- Subtle beats strong: boil ≈ 2–3% of the shape's size.

lessons.title: Claymation
lessons.summary: Soft 3D clay shading, cast shadows, flicker and miniature-set depth. Plasticine without the plasticine.
lessons.prompt: Make a 15-second claymation scene: a lavender clay blob character bounces onto a table, looks at the camera and blinks. Playful music, boing on each landing.
lessons.notes_md:
- Clay = soft radial lighting + darker rim + soft highlight + cast shadow.
- Add exposure flicker per drawing and blurred background layers for a "miniature set".
- Squash on landing, stretch while falling.

lessons.title: Crayon & hand-drawn
lessons.summary: Scribble fills, shaky double outlines and sketch-on reveals on warm paper.
lessons.prompt: Crayon-style 20-second explainer: a sun, a laptop and a coffee cup get sketched on, then coloured in, one per sentence of my voiceover.
lessons.notes_md:
- Outline drawn twice by a "shaky hand", then zig-zag hatched fill.
- Reveal = draw the outline on, then colour in.
- Fonts: Luckiest Guy, Gochi Hand, Caveat Brush.

lessons.title: Paper-cut & stop-motion
lessons.summary: Flat paper layers, drop shadows, parallax and torn-paper wipes.
lessons.notes_md:
- Flat colours + soft drop shadows between layers.
- Background layers move slower than foreground (parallax).
- Transitions: torn-paper shapes sliding across.

lessons.title: Characters that blink, look and talk
lessons.summary: Build a simple mascot rig: eyes that blink irregularly and look at things, a mouth that lip-syncs to the voice.
lessons.prompt: Give my mascot eyes that look at whatever is moving, natural blinks, and a mouth that talks along with work/vo.wav.
lessons.notes_md:
- Eyes look at the important thing **a beat before** the body moves.
- Irregular blinks feel alive. Regular blinks feel robotic.
- Lip-flap from the voice's loudness is convincing for cartoons.
- Keep characters "on model": same colours and proportions every shot.

lessons.title: Story structure for 30-second shorts
lessons.summary: Setup → problem → turn → payoff → end card. Plus gag timing that actually lands.
lessons.notes_md:
- 4–6 shots, ONE acting beat per shot.
- Gag = set-up → pause → hit (the hit on a beat with a sound).
- Readable with the sound off: clear poses and silhouettes.
- End card holds ≥ 2 s.

modules.title: AI Footage & Advanced VFX
modules.summary: Premium films from AI clips and phone footage: cut-outs, text behind you, tracking, cinematic looks, and AI footage that doesn't look AI.
modules.outcome: You can QC and assemble AI clips into a brand film, and add pro VFX to real footage, word-locked to speech.
modules.assignment: Either (A) a 45–60 second brand film from 5+ AI clips with voiceover and real graphics, or (B) a 20-second talking-head with 3 VFX moments triggered by your words.

lessons.title: Why AI clips look "AI" (and the fix)
lessons.summary: The 6 tell-tale artifacts of generated video and the editing habits that hide them.
lessons.notes_md:
- Tells: morphing hands/faces, garbled text, popping objects, melting geometry, flicker, too-smooth "plastic" look.
- Fix habits: short shots (1.5–4 s), cut before clips degrade, one grade + grain, real text and logos, real sound design.

lessons.title: Scan & select: QC every clip
lessons.summary: Automatic contact sheets and instability detection for every clip, then a usable-ranges list.
lessons.prompt: Scan all clips in raw/ and give me a table of which are usable, the exact usable ranges, and what's wrong with the rest.
lessons.notes_md:
- Review every sheet. The last 0.5–1 s of generated clips often degrades.
- Mark usable ranges → those become your edit list.
- Missing a shot? Ask for regeneration prompts or replace it with a graphic or real photo.

lessons.title: Assemble to the voiceover
lessons.summary: Map narration lines to shots, retime each shot to land on its words, and add transitions that don't feel cheap.
lessons.prompt: Cut the usable clips to my voiceover: one shot per sentence, cut on the key words, mostly hard cuts, fade only for time jumps.
lessons.notes_md:
- Keep speed changes between 0.7× and 1.4× so motion stays natural.
- Photos can be shots too (slow push-in = Ken Burns).
- Cut on the words that matter.

lessons.title: One grade to rule them all
lessons.summary: Unify mismatched clips with one look, film grain and a vignette. The single biggest "not AI" upgrade.
lessons.prompt: Grade everything with the same clean-bright look at 80%, add subtle grain and a light vignette. Show me before/after.
lessons.notes_md:
- Looks: natural, warm, cool, teal-orange, cinematic, moody, clean-bright, pastel, punchy, vintage, B&W, noir.
- Same look + same strength on every shot.
- A little grain hides the AI "plastic" smoothness.

lessons.title: Cut-outs & text behind you
lessons.summary: Remove or replace backgrounds and put giant text between you and the wall. The most viral VFX trick.
lessons.prompt: Put the word VIBE in huge lime letters behind me, appearing when I say "vibe", and replace the background with a soft blur.
lessons.notes_md:
- Best results: subject clearly separated from the background, good light, little motion blur.
- Best hair edges: the high-quality model (slower).
- Text behind subject = background → text → you on top.

lessons.title: Tracking, layers & "remove me"
lessons.summary: Stick graphics to a moving hand, split a shot into 3D-style layers, make yourself disappear into particles.
lessons.notes_md:
- **Tracking:** follow a point frame by frame and attach a logo/label. Hide it when tracking is lost.
- **Layer split:** background / you / text, separated with depth and parallax.
- **Remove me:** a clean empty background + you fading into particles.
- Be honest with clients: if an effect will look rough, offer a stylised alternative.

lessons.title: Cinematic looks, slow-mo & speed ramps
lessons.summary: Letterbox, film grade, serif titles, optical-flow slow motion and speed ramps.
lessons.prompt: Make it cinematic: 2.39 letterbox, teal-orange grade, slow push-in, serif titles, and slow-mo on the walk-in at 0:03.
lessons.notes_md:
- Optical-flow slow-mo is smooth on gentle motion. Fast motion can warp, so check stills.
- Speed ramp = normal → slow → normal across segments.
- On vertical video, use thin cinematic bars instead of full 2.39.

lessons.title: "Say it, it happens" edits
lessons.summary: The signature Vibe Editing reel: speak your edit directions on camera and every effect starts on the exact word.
lessons.prompt: In raw/take1.mp4 I say my edit directions out loud. Transcribe it and build each effect on the word that asks for it.
lessons.notes_md:
- Record with clear directions: "zoom in on my hand", "put my logo here", "remove me".
- Every effect starts on its trigger word and ends before the next.
- This format is a portfolio magnet. Make one for yourself.

lessons.title: Faceless channels: script → episode
lessons.summary: A repeatable pipeline: script, AI voice, visuals per sentence, pop captions, music and export.
lessons.prompt: Turn work/script.txt into a 60-second faceless Short: AI voice, one visual per sentence, pop captions, tech music bed, export for Shorts and Reels.
lessons.notes_md:
- Script: hook line, 3 points, CTA. Written as spoken.
- Save the pipeline as a one-command script → every new episode is "write script, run".
- Batch many episodes with the Bulk skill (Bulk, Workflow & Getting Paid module).

modules.title: Bulk, Workflow & Getting Paid
modules.summary: Turn the skill into income: bulk production, delivery that looks professional, pricing, proposals and your portfolio.
modules.outcome: You have a portfolio, a price list, a proposal template and a delivery workflow, and you've completed a client-style capstone.
modules.assignment: Capstone: complete a full client-style job (brief → beat table → stills approval → render → 1 revision → multi-platform delivery) and submit the folder + final videos.

lessons.title: Bulk videos from a spreadsheet
lessons.summary: One hero template → 100 personalised videos. Test 3 rows, then render the rest with a report.
lessons.prompt: Make a personalised welcome video for every row in students.csv using first_name and course. Test the first 3 rows before rendering all.
lessons.notes_md:
- Collect samples including the **longest** names. That's where templates break.
- Clean data first: spaces, capitals, empty fields, duplicates.
- The report lists every video: ok / skipped / failed.
- 💰 Personalised video is a premium service: sales outreach, onboarding, events.

lessons.title: One edit → every format & language
lessons.summary: 9:16, 4:5, 1:1 and 16:9 from one design, plus translated voiceover and captions per language.
lessons.notes_md:
- Design in relative units → re-render per format → check stills.
- Translation: same number of sentences so timings hold.
- Non-Latin scripts need the right fonts (Devanagari, Japanese...).
- Always have a native speaker check one version.

lessons.title: Render faster: drafts, sections & templates
lessons.summary: Stills in seconds, half-res drafts, rendering just one section, and turning past projects into templates.
lessons.notes_md:
- Stills → draft → final. Never full-render to check a typo.
- Render only the changed section when fixing one moment.
- Every finished project is a template: *"Save this style so the next one is a one-liner."*

lessons.title: Delivery like a pro
lessons.summary: File naming, platform exports, subtitles, thumbnails, contact sheets and licence notes.
lessons.notes_md:
- Names: `client_project_format_v2.mp4`.
- Deliver: platform exports + `.srt` + thumbnail still + contact sheet.
- Note licences: fonts (OFL), music (generated original), footage source.
- Keep every version. Never overwrite what the client has seen.

lessons.title: Pricing your Vibe Editing services
lessons.summary: Packages, per-video vs retainer pricing, and how to price on value, not hours, when AI does the heavy lifting.
lessons.notes_md:
- Sell **outcomes and turnaround**, not hours. Your speed is your margin.
- Typical packages: Reel pack (8–12 reels/month), Launch kit (promo + variants + cut-downs), Motion pack (titles + lower-thirds), Personalised campaign (per-video pricing at volume).
- Always include: revision rounds (2), formats, turnaround time.
- Retainers > one-offs.

lessons.title: Proposals, briefs & client communication
lessons.summary: A one-page proposal, a brief the client fills, and the update rhythm that makes clients trust you.
lessons.notes_md:
- Proposal: their goal → your plan → deliverables → timeline → price → next step.
- Send the brief template before the first call.
- Every update = file + contact sheet + 1–3 specific questions.

lessons.title: Build your portfolio in a weekend
lessons.summary: The 6 portfolio pieces that cover what clients buy, and how to package them into a showreel.
lessons.notes_md:
1. A talking-head reel with pop captions
2. A launch promo + 1:1 variant
3. A logo reveal
4. A stylised short (clay/crayon)
5. A "say it, it happens" VFX reel
6. A before/after (raw vs edited)
- Cut your best 3 seconds of each into a 30-second showreel (see the Motion Graphics module).

lessons.title: Capstone: a full client-style project
lessons.summary: Put it all together: brief → beat table → stills → draft → final → revision → multi-platform delivery.
lessons.notes_md:
- Pick a real business (a friend's café, your own brand, a local gym).
- Submit: brief.md, beat table, contact sheets, final exports, revisions log.
- Graded on: hook strength, clarity, brand consistency, sound, delivery quality.
- 🏆 Top capstones get featured on the Ideabro Studio page.
